Container.Name: copilot-cli
Container.Overview: GitHub Copilot CLI with sidebar terminals, Node.js, Python, persistent tools and optional GPU access.
Container.Description:
A browser terminal for GitHub Copilot CLI and GitHub CLI, backed by persistent Alpine Linux storage.
Set a strong web terminal password, then open the WebUI. The terminal supports colors, copy/paste, and interactive applications. Map /config to Appdata. GitHub and Copilot credentials, configuration, caches, and packages installed with `apk add` persist there. Storage/repos is mounted at /Storage/repos and is the starting directory for every connection. Open multiple terminals from the left sidebar to run concurrent tasks. Switching keeps tasks running. All terminals share the same GitHub sign-in, files, permissions and installed tools. Node.js and Python are included. Python pip packages, global npm tools, authentication and the encrypted system keyring persist in /config. Alpine packages installed with apk add are restored on container recreation. The optional GPU device entry exposes /dev/dri without privileged mode; remove it if not needed or unavailable. Both web terminal credentials are customizable below. These are separate from your GitHub account. The terminal runs as root inside the container; do not expose it directly to the internet.

Config.Name: Persistent configuration
Config.Description: Stores authentication, keyring, settings, the shared Python environment, global npm tools, caches and the list of additional APK packages.

Config.Name: Repositories
Config.Description: Storage share repositories folder. Every new terminal starts here; other Storage folders are not exposed.

Config.Name: Web terminal username
Config.Description: Choose the username for WebUI sign-in. Editable here; this is not your GitHub username.

Config.Name: Web terminal password
Config.Description: Choose a strong WebUI password. Editable here and separate from your GitHub credentials and keyring unlock secret.

Config.Name: GPU device (optional)
Config.Description: Intel/AMD GPU access without privileged mode. Remove this device entry to disable, especially on hosts without /dev/dri; do not leave it blank. GPU workloads may need additional userspace libraries.
